title: A Comprehensive Study of Implicit and Explicit Biases in Large Language Models
findings: Models were evaluated for religious bias using stereotype detection benchmarks (StereoSet and CrowS-Pairs). The study found that models exhibited biases, and their performance varied. For instance, in explicit bias prompting on the CrowS-Pairs dataset, DistilBERT was the least biased model (29% stereotype selection) while GPT-3.5 was the most biased (79%). Fine-tuning and data augmentation strategies were employed to mitigate these biases, with mixed results. A Bag-of-Words analysis revealed specific keywords that influenced the models' stereotypical choices related to religion, such as 'terrorists', 'holy', and 'vedas'. The paper also noted a previous study that specifically compared religious bias between Islam and other languages.
